title: Word Search II
spaceBreakdown:
- Trie nodes: up to total characters of all words → O(T)  
- recursion depth: at most L → O(L)  
- result vector: at most number of words → O(words) (not counted per statement)  
- not counted: input board, input word list
approach:
All words are stored in a Trie so that common prefixes are shared.  
From each cell we run a DFS that follows only edges existing in the Trie; when a Trie node marks the end of a word we add it to the answer and delete the word from the Trie to prevent duplicates.  
Because the search stops as soon as the current path is not a prefix of any word, the total work is bounded by the board size times the maximum word length.
hints:
When many words share common prefixes, how can we avoid exploring the same board paths repeatedly for each word?  
Each word length is at most 10.

Use a **Trie (prefix tree)** to store all words.  
Starting from board[0][0] = ‘o’, the path o → a → t → h in the Trie leads to the word “oath”.

buildTrie(words)  
for each cell (i,j) on board

**Single‑cell board** - the board contains only one letter and words are length 1.  
`Input: board = [['a']], words = ["a","b"]` → `Expected: ["a"]`  
⚠️ Bug: stopping DFS only when the cell is out of bounds → returns `["a","b"]`.

**Word longer than board** - a word cannot be formed because its length exceeds total cells.  
`Input: board = [["a","b"],["c","d"]], words = ["abcdc"]` → `Expected: []`  
⚠️ Bug: not checking visited flag and allowing reuse of a cell → may incorrectly return `["abcdc"]`.

**All words share full board as prefix** - many words start with the same long prefix that covers the whole board.  
`Input: board = [["a","a"],["a","a"]], words = ["aa","aaa","aaaa"]` → `Expected: ["aa","aaa","aaaa"]`  
⚠️ Bug: clearing the word flag after first discovery without preserving deeper words → returns only `["aa"]`.

followUps.q: What if the board size can be up to 100 × 100 while word length stays ≤10?
followUps.a: The same Trie‑guided DFS works; the time becomes O(m·n·L) = O(10⁴·10) which is fine. Memory is still O(T).

followUps.q: How would you modify the solution if the list of words could contain duplicates?
followUps.a: Store a counter in each Trie node for how many times the word appears; when the node is reached, push the word that many times and set the counter to 0 to avoid further repeats. Complexity stays unchanged.

followUps.q: Suppose the board cannot be modified in‑place (no marking with ‘#’). How can you still achieve O(1) extra space per call?
followUps.a: Keep a separate boolean visited matrix of size m·n; it adds O(m·n) auxiliary space, still acceptable because m·n ≤ 144 in the original constraints. The algorithmic complexity does not change.
